page: UpCloud GPU-12xCPU-128GB-2xL4 is a GPU-accelerated virtual server built on the KVM hypervisor. The system features 12 vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor using the x86_64 architecture. This configuration provides 12 physical cores with a thread-per-core ratio of 1.0 under a shared CPU allocation model. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding 10.67 GB of RAM per core. Graphics processing is handled by two NVIDIA L4 GPUs from the Ada Lovelace family, delivering a combined 48 GB of VRAM. No local storage is bundled with this instance type, though it includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier single-core CPU performance, with a stress-ng single-core score of 3942.28 and top-tier single-threaded compression speeds, including 42.79 GB/sec in gzip compression and 19.58 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression. Multi-core CPU performance and memory bandwidth fall within the average tier. For artificial intelligence workloads, the server achieves top-tier text generation speeds of 349.81 tokens/sec during small model LLM inference, while prompt processing speeds remain in the average tier.

This server configuration offers high resource density by pairing dual enterprise GPUs with a substantial memory footprint. It represents a qualitatively cost-efficient option for workloads requiring high VRAM and memory capacity without the overhead of local storage. The hardware profile is suited for machine learning inference, data science operations, and single-thread intensive compute tasks.
